subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in core hold/retract mechanism for forwarded exec approvals, and what exact config/protocol/security contract should it expose?
rationale: The requested behavior changes a human approval safety boundary and public config/protocol surface, so automation should not choose the product and security semantics on its own.

options.title: Design core hold/retract
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored design that preserves fail-open prompt delivery, fail-closed execution, and auditable retractions.

options.title: Reject the feature
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide immediate human visibility is a stronger invariant than suppressing agent-abandoned prompts.

options.title: Defer to a narrower API discussion
options.body: Track only the missing approval-extension API if maintainers want plugin or client experiments before committing to `holdMs` in core config.

recommendation.title: Design core hold/retract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored design that preserves fail-open prompt delivery, fail-closed execution, and auditable retractions.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged approval-framework work is the closest history for choosing the shared approval manager/protocol boundary.
